RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the August 4, 2006/Sravana 6, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Agriculture; Agro and Rural Industries; Chemicals and Fertilizers;
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests;

Total number of questions —20
Revival plan for sick fertilizer units
*181. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are working on a proposal to revive eight
sick or closed public sector fertilizer
factories in the country;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal and
estimated time frame alongwith the cost
for the revival;
(c) whether the revival of these factories
will be sufficient to meet the growing
demand of fertilizers in the country; and
(d) if not, in what way Government
propose to meet the excess demand?
Malaria control in North Eastern
Region
*182. SHRI SILVIUS CONDPAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has established
a wing at Guwahati to control/fight malaria
epidemic affecting the lives of the people
of North Eastern States every year
resulting in loss of lives of poor villagers;
(b) what was the amount sanctioned
during 2004-05 and 2005-06 for Assam to
combat AIDS/HIV cases; and
(c) what are the actions taken by the
State Government in this connection?
Security arrangements at stations
†*183. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:
SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that despite bomb
explosions in Mumbai no strict arrange-
ments of security on various railway
stations including the capital have been made;
(b) if so, whether it is also a fact that at
the most important station of the capital,
most of the door metal detectors are either
out of order or not functioning properly;
(c) if so, whether Government propose
to take steps to improve the security
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
arrangements on various railway stations
including those of the capital; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Stoppage of wastage and value
addition under horticulture
mission
*184. SHRI EKANATH K.
THAKUR: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Rs. 15,000
crore horticulture mission is taking big
steps forward as agricultural scientists are
coming up with do's and don'ts for
preventing the colossal waste of fruits and
vegetables in the country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that
agricultural scientists are working on the
linkages for intensifying efforts for value
addition in fruits and vegetables as part of
the horticulture mission; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Second Green Revolution
†*185. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI MANGANI LAL
MANDAL:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Chairman
of National Commission on Farmers, Dr.
M.S. Swaminathan has underlined the need
for Second Green Revolution in the
country;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard;
(c) whether it is also a fact that there is
need of making dry land or land dependent
on rain useful upto the maximum level in
order to bring Second Green Revolution in
the country;
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto; and
(e) the scheme being prepared by
Government for Second Green Revolution?
Vacancies in Indian Council of
Agricultural Research
*186. SHRIMATI  SYEDA
ANWARA TAIMUR:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) how many posts of scientific nature
are vacant in the Indian Council of
Agricultural Research;
(b) the reasons for not filling these
posts;
(c) whether keeping so many posts
vacant has not hindered the progress of
various research schemes; and
(d) how long it would take to fill all
these vacant posts?
Wastage of stored wheat and rice
†*187. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) the quantity of grains deteriorated
out of wheat and rice stocked by the Food
Corporation of India during the last three
years, year-wise;
(b) the quantity of wheat used as animal
feed out of it and the quantity which was
not fit even for the said purpose; and
(c) the details of scheme by the Central
Government in order to improve the storage
system?

58
Directive for participation of
corporates in 'Green Drive'
*188. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether on the World Environment
Day, Government had given a call to
corporates to play a greater role in 'Green
Drive' in a whole range of issues from
forestry to naming affluent plants and
monitoring the pollution; and
(b) if so, the response of different
sectors of industry, like pesticides, dyes
and chemicals, pharmaceuticals, distilleries,
cement, mines and metals, to this directive?
Appointment with consultants by
CGHS beneficiaries
*189. SHRIMATI  MOHSINA
KIDWAI:
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government Officers of
certain level are allowed to have direct
appointments with consultants/specialists
as CGHS beneficiaries in hospitals in
Delhi;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the mechanism in place through
which appointments can be had;
(d) whether Government propose to
devise a procedure whereby such officers
can have specialist consultation through
appointments; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Misuse of CGHS facility
*190. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it has come to the
knowledge of Government that there is a
rampant misuse and abuse of the facility
provided to the beneficiaries of CGH
Scheme to get themselves treated from the
privately run hospitals recognized by the
Central Government; and
(b) if so, the steps Government propose
to take to minimize or eliminate misuse
and abuse of this facility?
Preparedness for locust invasion
*191. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have informed
the FAO that it was prepared for a possible
locust invasion;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the present position thereof?
Forest dwellers
*192. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) the number of forest dwellers having
no order of settlement in the country,
State-wise;
(b) how many of them belong to
Scheduled Tribes;
(c) whether Government are going to
relax the rules in order to facilitate these
families for the use of forest produces under
some control; and
(d) the details of the programme of
Government?

59
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Retrieval of railway land from
encroachers
*193. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to refer
to the answer to Unstarred Question 3013
given in the Rajya Sabha on the 12th May,
2006 and state:
(a) the number of cases with the area of
land in each case with location thereof which
the Railways were able to retrieve from
encroachers during the last three years
ending 31st March, 2006; and
(b) the number of cases with location
thereof for which the railway administration
has initiated action under Public Premises
(Eviction of Unauthorized Occupants) Act,
1971 and the Railways Act, 1989?
Prescribing expensive medicines
*194. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELF ARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
most of the doctors and medical
practitioners prescribe highly expensive
medicines which are sometimes beyond the
reach of common men;
(b) if so, the remedial measures
Government propose to take to check such
exploitation of patients and referring them
to particular labs, clinics/hospitals for tests
or hospitalization, etc.; and
(c) whether any agency already exists
in order to monitor and regulate such unfair
means adopted by the medical practitioners
and if so, the details thereof?
Crashworthy impact reducing coaches
*195. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to
bring out "crashworthy" i.e. impact-
reducing coaches with anti-climbing
features to reduce the impact of collision
and provide maximum safety to the
passengers;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the time-frame within which these
coaches would be added to the rakes to
control loss of life and property in rail
accidents?
Reduction in wheat quota for BPL and
Antyodaya households
*196. SHRI C. PERUMAL:
MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to reduce the
wheat earmarked for Below Poverty Line
(BPL) and Antyodaya households; and
(b) if so, the reasons therefor?
Heritage train in Uttar Pradesh
*197. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
Government of Uttar Pradesh has suggested
the introduction of a "heritage train" to
attract especially the foreign tourists to the
State which has, amongst others, the world
famous Taj Mahal, India's biggest draw,
besides some world heritage sites and a large
number of other centres of tourist interest;

60
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the details of the proposals
received and the present status of its
consideration/implementation; and
(c) the details of proposals received/
under consideration, if any, for introduction
of such dedicated special trains in other
States or between States to cover important
tourists circuits in the country?
Promoting bio-fertilizers
†*198. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether research has revealed that
the production capacity of land is not
reduced as a result of increasing the quantity
of bio-fertilizers;
(b) if so, the steps being taken to
promote it comprehensively and
intensively; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Enhancing procurement of wheat
†*199. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has
been less procurement of wheat by
Government in the country than its
requirement during the year 2005-06;
(b) if so, the facts thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
quantity of Government procurement of
wheat could be enhanced by further
increasing its purchase-price;
(d) if so, Government's reaction thereto;
and
(e) the reasons for not taking measures
by Government in this direction?
Surrender of posts relating to safety
*200. SHRIMATI  N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the reasons that various divisions of
the Indian Railways have surrendered
1.90 lakh posts belonging to safety category
between 2001 and 2006;
(b) whether it is also a fact that 500
posts again belonging to safety category
have been surrendered in Vijayawada
Division alone during the last five years;
(c) if so, whether it would not affect the
safety of the Railways which is being
criticized due to a lot of accidents and put
more pressure on the existing staff which
hinders their efficiency; and
(d) looking at the whole scenario,
whether Government are considering to
avoid surrendering of posts and fill up the
posts of important categories like safety?

Vehicular pollution
1174. SHRI S.P.M. SYED KHAN: Will
the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:

vehicles in the country the vehicular
pollution load has gone up eight times in
twenty years indicating a dire warning;
(b) the steps taken by Government
especially, to curb the air pollution keeping
in the view the increased use of vehicles;
and
(c) Government's policy on advanced
technology solutions for the automobile
industries to control air pollution?
Import of wheat
1175. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have decided
to import wheat recently;
(b) if so, the details thereof;

our country in the last five years, year-
wise and State-wise;
(d) the details of wheat procurement
by Government and its agencies, year-wise
and State-wise;
(e) the MSP offered to the wheat
farmers, year-wise;

wise;

Milk production

SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:

in the total production of milk in the
country;

Employment opportunities in

MISHRA:
SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:
SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE

in agricultural and its ancillary sectors are
continuously diminishing;

Seed and fertilizers subsidy to
farmers

equally to small and marginal farmers;

distributing the subsidy; and
(d) the programmes launched by
Government to educate the farmers in
adopting modern agricultural technology?
Implementation of NAIS
1180. SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI VINAY KATIYAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE

(a) the States and the Union Territories
where the National Agricultural Insurance
Scheme (NAIS) has not been implemented;
(b) the details thereof and the reasons
therefor;
(c) the time by which this scheme is
likely to be implemented in all the States;
and
(d) the details of the insurance
companies implementing NAIS?

272

Promotion of horticulture in Assam
1181. SHRI DWIJENDRA NATH
SHARMAH: Will the Minister of

(a) the details of areas identified in the

and
(b) the details of financial assistance

years?
Mobile storage for containting
wastage of foodstuffs
1182. SHRI SANJAY RAUT: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that more than
Rs. 50,000 crore of agricultural foodstuffs
are lost annually in the country;
(b) if so, the strategy Government
would like to take in this respect;
(c) whether Government would like to
make available mobile storage at every
village;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

1183. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE  be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of amount provided under
the National Horticulture Mission to
Uttaranchal during the Tenth Five Year Plan,
year-wise;
(b) whether the potential belt has been
identified in the State to cover the same
under the mission; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Changes in agricultural land use

JOSHI:
SHRI RAVI SHANKAR
PRASAD:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the use of
agricultural land is being changed on a large
scale in various States of the country;
(b) if so, the facts thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that agricultural
land is decreasing due to change in its
utilisation;
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto; and
(e) whether Government would
formulate a National Land Use Policy to
ban the change in the utilisation of
agricultural land?

second green revolution

SINGH MAJITHA: Will the Minister of

(a) whether new agricultural policy
would be formulated by Government to
bring second green revolution in the
country;
(b) if so, by when it is likely to be
announced; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?

RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE  be pleased to state:
(a) the details of farmers, crops and
agricultural land covered under National
Agricultural Insurance Scheme (NAIS) in
Andhra Pradesh, till date;
(b) the criteria followed to decide the
rate of premium under the scheme, crop-
wise;
(c) the details of financial liabilities
shared by Central Government and the
States/Union Territories;
(d) the total amount of premium
collected for the said scheme in the State
during each of the last three years; and
(e) the payment made against the
insurance claims during the said period, till
date?
Functioning of CACP
1187. SHRI C. RAMACHAND-
RAIAH: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE  be pleased to state:
(a) the role of Commission for
Agricultural Costs and Prices in fixing the
prices of foodgrains;
(b) whether the said Commission is
functioning properly;
(c) whether Government are ignoring
the recommendations of the said
Commission;
(d) if so, the reasons therefor;
(e) the steps taken by Government to
provide remunerative prices to the farmers;
and
(f) the success achieved by Government
in this regard?
Enhancing NDRI's credibility
1188. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that for the last
over a decade, no Dairy Technologist has
been recruited in NDRI, Karnal, Haryana;
(b) if so, whether an impression is
gaining ground among the students
that there is no employment
opportunity for the Research Scholars
passing out with Ph.D. degree in
Dairy Technology within and outside
NDRI, Karnal; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and measures
taken by Government to enhance NDRI's
credibility so as to boost the employment
prospects in the market for their students
holding doctorate degree in Dairy
Technology?
Projects for agricultural research and
education

BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
AGRICULTURE  be pleased to state:

AGRICULTURE  research and education
in agricultural science have been approved
at a cost of  Rs. 1190 crores to give strong
impetus to agricultural research;
(b) if so, whether six-year project
involving a $ 200 million credit line from
World Bank would be implemented from
1st July, 2006;

274
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) whether Government have approved
Rs. 200 crores more over and above
Rs. 720 crores allocated for improving
agricultural education for remaining period
of the Tenth Five Year Plan; and
(d) if so, to what extent these projects
would help in production, consumption
system and achieving other objectives?
Abnormal pricing practice by Bt.
Seed companies
1190. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether complaints have been
received on behalf of farming community
against the abnormal pricing practice by
Bt. Seed companies;
(b) if so, whether any action has been
initiated against the companies;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Work plan of India-US Knowledge
Initiative
1191. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE  be
pleased to state:
(a) the detailed work plan of India-US
Knowledge Initiative on AGRICULTURE
, Agricultural Education, Research and
Commercial Linkage;
(b) whether the Knowledge Initiative
focuses on introduction of GMO's and
irradiated foods in India at a time when
the world is recognizing the productivity
and ecological sustainability of small
farmer; and
(c) how much India will be benefited
by adopting sustainable and hazardous
technology through the US-India
Agriculture Agreement?
Decrease in milch cattle
†1192. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE  be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the number of milching
animals is decreasing swiftly in the
country;
(b) if so, the main reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government have made
any review of losses caused to economy
due to reduction in livestock;
(d) whether the livestock is being
stealthily exported from the country to
Bangladesh, etc.; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Research activities on agricultural
production
1193. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether ICAR has carried out
agricultural research activities in various
States with a view to increase agricultural
production;
(b) if so, the research activities
undertaken in various parts of the country

three years;
(c) the recommendations of ICAR for
increasing agricultural production in Tamil
Nadu; and
(d) the follow-up action initiated by
Government thereon?
Increase in rural landless families
1194. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number
of rural landless families have increased from
35 per cent between 1987 and 1998 to 55
per cent between 2003 and 2005;
(b) if so, whether any study has been
done in this regard;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the reasons for the increase in the
number of rural landless families and
Government's reaction thereto?
Coverage under crop insurance scheme
1195. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE  be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of farmers' families
brought under crop insurance scheme in
different States of the country;
(b) the percentage of coverage by crop
insurance scheme, State-wise; and
(c) the extension of benefits
contemplated by Government for the poor
and marginal farmers?
MSP of wheat and paddy
†1196. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) to what extent increase in the MSP
of wheat and paddy has been made during
the last five years, year-wise and to what
extent cost price of farming has increased;
(b) whether the loss caused to farmers
due to drought and flood is also taken into
account while fixing MSP;
(c) the per quintal price of wheat
imported from abroad alongwith the per
quintal transportation expenses thereof;
(d) the quantity of wheat procured by
Government last year and during the current
financial year, separately; and
(e) the reasons for meagre purchase?
Coverage area of Bt. cotton
1197. SHRIMATI N.P DURGA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has
now become a major player in the transgenic
crops by achieving coverage area of 50,000
hectares;
(b) whether it is also a fact that India
has hiked its Bt. Cotton area coverage by
400 per cent between 2002-04;
(c) if so, the percentage of increase in
Andhra Pradesh since introduction of Bt.
Cotton in the country; and
(d) in what manner Government are
planning to galvanise the global biotech crop
market in the next three years?

276
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Compensation to poultry farmers of
Maharashtra
1198. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of poultry farms working
in Maharashtra and the investment made
therein as on date;
(b) whether it is a fact that the poultry
farmers have started committing suicide due
to non-payment of compensation at the
rate of Rs. 20/- declared by the State
Government because of Bird Flu epidemic;
(c) how much loss is estimated due to
Bird Flu epidemic slaughter of hens and
reduced rate of meat to poultry farmers;
and
(d) the steps taken to provide relief
and rehabilitation to poultry farmers of
Maharashtra?
Time limit for payment under crop
insurance scheme
†1199. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
